chapter: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
title: The rhythm and blues tour of the South
summary: After the Cavalcade he led a small band with Larry Darnell and Wynonie Harris, playing crowds of 4,000-5,000 black audiences across the South.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah, that would be interesting. I'm going to just -- after the Cavalcade of Jazz, Eddie, is this right, that you lead a small touring band with vocalist (inaudible) Harris and Larry Darnelle. What sort of singer was Larry Darnelle?
He was a blues singer. He could sing (inaudible) Johnny Mathis. (Inaudible.)
And (inaudible) would take care of the rougher blues.
What sort of audiences were you playing to, mostly blacks?
I mean, that was designed for that.
Yeah, only the whites would crash (inaudible). We were playing crowds of 4,000, 5,000.
about 12 cities in Florida, South Carolina, North Carolina, everywhere, all the states (inaudible) the South -- Florida, Key West.
(Inaudible). We would drive two cars, and I had a nine-passenger DeSoto (inaudible). And I had a trailer, a steel trailer (inaudible).
Who did you have in the band?
It was (inaudible) to be towards the rhythm and blues.
(Inaudible.) Had good musicians. We used tenor, trumpet and trombone.
